candidates.title: The 3% Battery Rescue
candidates.one_line_concept: Aachu and Zuv do not say anything romantic; one just silently passes the charger across the bed before the other's phone dies.
candidates.emotional_truth: Long-term tenderness often looks like noticing a tiny emergency before it becomes annoying.
candidates.relatable_trigger: The shared charger that somehow belongs to both people but is always needed by the one farther from the socket.
candidates.visual_evidence: Low battery screen, tangled cable across the bedsheet, one half-asleep hand offering the charger, two mugs or books left unfinished nearby.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Low if the carousel focuses on the silent timing, the awkward cable stretch, and the tiny relieved look instead of a generic 'you care for me' line.

candidates.title: The Rewatch Treaty
candidates.one_line_concept: One of them falls asleep during a show, and the other quietly rewinds tomorrow and pretends they also forgot what happened.
candidates.emotional_truth: Love can be choosing shared experience over being technically right.
candidates.relatable_trigger: The tiny guilt of watching ahead versus the sweetness of saving the story for both of you.
candidates.visual_evidence: Paused streaming screen, blanket slipping, one sleepy head on the other's shoulder, next-day cups beside the same scene replaying.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium-low; it needs the specific pretending-not-to-know beat to avoid becoming a standard cozy TV couple scene.

candidates.title: The Last Bite Negotiation
candidates.one_line_concept: Aachu and Zuv both claim they are full, then spend three slides protecting the exact last bite the other secretly wants.
candidates.emotional_truth: Knowing someone's food preferences becomes a private language.
candidates.relatable_trigger: The final crispy corner, extra chutney, or best spoonful that couples silently track for each other.
candidates.visual_evidence: One plate between them, two spoons paused mid-air, the best bite moved to the other's side, a shared laugh after both get caught caring.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium; food-sharing is common, so it must hinge on a very specific bite preference rather than broad 'sharing is love.'

candidates.title: The Same-Room Text
candidates.one_line_concept: They are sitting two feet apart, but one texts the other a tiny request or meme because speaking would ruin the comfortable silence.
candidates.emotional_truth: Some couples become so safe together that silence is not distance; it is home.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Texting 'water?' or sending a ridiculous reel while sitting in the same room.
candidates.visual_evidence: Two phones lighting up, crossed legs on opposite ends of a sofa, one raised eyebrow, one suppressed smile, a glass of water arriving without a word.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Low if the carousel keeps the request oddly specific and avoids making it only a meme joke.

candidates.title: The Doorway Checklist
candidates.one_line_concept: They are already leaving, but one pauses at the door and the other automatically names the forgotten thing before being asked.
candidates.emotional_truth: Real intimacy is remembering each other's tiny chaos without turning it into a complaint.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Keys, wallet, charger, lip balm, water bottle, lights, gas, AC: the couple exit ritual everyone quietly has.
candidates.visual_evidence: One shoe half-worn, keys in hand, tote bag open, charger still plugged in, the other person holding the missing item with a knowing face.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium; it can become sitcom nagging unless both people are shown as mutually forgetful and mutually caring.

top_pick.title: The 3% Battery Rescue
top_pick.reason: It has the strongest mix of tiny observed behavior, immediate visual proof, low stereotype risk, and tender payoff without needing a dramatic line or polished romance.

rejected_patterns: Generic 'home is a person' couple quote
Perfect partner who always knows everything
Boy forgets, girl fixes it dynamic
Aesthetic cuddling without a behavioral detail
risk_notes: Keep care mutual across Aachu and Zuv so the carousel does not assign emotional labor to one person.
Use everyday props as proof, not decoration.
Avoid captions that explain the lesson too directly; the behavior should carry the feeling.
Do not over-romanticize the scenes into fantasy luxury interiors; the charm is the recognizable micro-moment.
